text:
maria: Quick design thread  proposing a "slimline" left rail where 'Serving' replaces separate Models + Deployments. New ideas: keyboard shortcuts to jump to top-level groups (g then s -> Serving), and a small breadcrumb variant that shows "Serving / <panel>" with an expand-to-reveal workspace trail. Thoughts?

dan: Hotkeys sound great, especially for power users. We should make them discoverable (tooltip in command palette) and configurable. Also: what should happen if someone opens a deep link that points to an old /models path?

kofi: Routing: accept old paths as aliases and normalize to canonical /org/:o/ws/:w/serving/:panel with replaceState on first load so the URL in the address bar updates without stacking history. For user-initiated nav, pushState. We'll also emit 301s for external requests server-side.

helena: Accessibility: hotkeys must be documented and not conflict with browser/AT shortcuts. When a hotkey opens a panel, move focus to the panel heading and announce via aria-live: "Serving, <panel> opened". Keyboard-only users must be able to reveal the full breadcrumb trail with a focusable control.

maria: Good. For the breadcrumb pill reveal, we should use a menu button with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded, not hover. The expanded trail should be reachable via arrow keys.

dan: For migration messaging, proposing two A/B toast copy options shown once per user when they hit an alias for the first time:
A) "We grouped Models and Deployments under 'Serving'. Your bookmarks will keep working for 60 days. Learn more."
B) "Models + Deployments are now in 'Serving'. Bookmarks still work for 60 days. View migration guide."
Which do we prefer? Short vs explicit?

kofi: I prefer A (clear sentence, action link). Also add an opt-out "Don't show again" that sets a user preference. Accessibility: ensure the toast has role/status and remains focusable for keyboard users to dismiss.

helena: Toast note: avoid passive voice and be explicit about the timeframe. Also ensure the toast doesn't trap focus and that screen readers announce it. Use aria-live polite but ensure the link is reachable.

dan: Implementation sketch for the alias table (very small):
```
/org/:o/ws/:w/models -> client replaceState -> /org/:o/ws/:w/serving/models (emit telemetry alias_redirect)
/org/:o/ws/:w/deployments -> client replaceState -> /org/:o/ws/:w/serving/deployments
Legacy routes accepted for 60 days, then 301 -> canonical
```

maria: Also want a small UX polish: when canonicalizing, we can show a subtle snackbar "Using new location: Serving / Models" that auto-dismisses. Keep the migration toast separate (only first-time).

kofi: Telemetry to track: alias_redirect_count, canonicalize_replace_rate, hotkey_usage, breadcrumb_pill_expand_rate, toast_dismiss_rate. Feature flag the rail change and hotkeys for safe rollback.

helena: Additional a11y nit: when we collapse org/ws into a pill, truncated labels must have aria-label with the full name and the expand control should expose that via aria-describedby. Also test with VoiceOver and NVDA for announcing the pill expansion.

dan: Keyboard flows: define a mnemonic system for rails (g then s for Serving, g then o for Observability). Document in the command palette and in the keyboard shortcuts page. Make sure modifiers are configurable.

maria: Motion guidance: rail group expand/collapse should be a short 100ms transform (no layout shift), breadcrumb reveal should fade+translate 120ms. Avoid large repaints.

build-bot: Canary preview is live: https://canary.console.redwood.ai/slimline-rail (SSO required).

kofi: QA plan: unit tests for route normalization, integration test for back-button behaviour, E2E for deep-link + auth redirect preserving anchor, and manual keyboard/a11y pass.

maria: I'll draft small mocks, hotkey spec, and the alias mapping spreadsheet. Will post a short copy doc with the toast A/B options and recommended single winner. Tagging @helena for the a11y checklist. Thanks all!
_reserved: do not add extra nested fields
